title: New Leader Alert: Joshua Steps Up
paragraphs: So, after Moses, God's servant, passed away, God hit up Joshua, Moses's assistant. He was like:

"Yo, my servant Moses is gone. It's your turn now. Get up and cross the Jordan River, you and this whole crew. You're heading to the land I'm giving the people of Israel. For real, every single place you step, it's yours—I already promised this to Moses. From the desert and Lebanon all the way east to the big Euphrates River—the whole Hittite area—and then west to the Mediterranean Sea. It's all for you. All your life, no one's gonna be able to stand against you, like, ever. Just like I had Moses's back, I've got yours. I'm not gonna bail on you or leave you hanging. Be strong. Be brave. You're the one who's gonna lead these people to get the land I swore to their ancestors I'd give them. So go all in, heart and soul. Make sure you follow every single rule Moses gave you from me. Don't get sidetracked, not even a little, so you can actually get where you're going. And don't let this Book of the Law out of your sight for a second. Think about it 24/7, and actually do what it says. Then you'll make it, for real. You'll be successful. Didn't I tell you? Be strong! Be brave! Don't be scared or freaked out. Your God is with you literally every step of the way."

Then Joshua told the leaders of the people, "Go through the camp and tell everyone to pack their stuff. In three days, we're crossing the Jordan River to go in and take the land our God is giving us."

Then Joshua talked to the guys from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He said, "Remember what Moses, God's servant, told you: Your God is giving you a place to chill, and he's giving you this land. Your wives, kids, and animals can stay here east of the Jordan, the land Moses gave you. But all you soldiers have to cross the river ready for a fight, leading your brothers to help them out. You gotta help them until their God gives them a place to rest just like he did for you. They'll also take over the land their God is giving them. After that, you can come back to your own land that Moses, God's servant, gave you over here east of the Jordan."

They answered Joshua, "Whatever you say, we'll do. Wherever you send us, we'll go. We followed Moses completely, and we'll follow you too. We just pray that your God will be with you like he was with Moses. Anyone who questions you or refuses to do what you say will be put to death. So be strong and brave!"

title: Two Spies & A Secret Promise
paragraphs: So, Joshua, Nun's son, lowkey sent two dudes out from Shittim as spies. He was like, "Go check out the land, especially Jericho." So they bounced and ended up at the house of a prostitute named Rahab and crashed there for the night.
Word got to the king of Jericho, like, "Yo, some Israelite guys just showed up tonight to spy on our land."
The king of Jericho hit up Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to your house tonight. They're spies, here to scope out the whole country."

But the woman had already taken the two men and hidden them. She was like, "Yeah, two guys came by, but I didn't know where they were from. They left around dusk, right when the gate was about to close. I have no idea where they went. But if you hurry, you might still catch them!" (Plot twist: she had actually taken them up to the roof and hidden them under a pile of flax she had laid out.) So the king's men chased them down the road toward the Jordan River fords. As soon as the pursuers left, they shut the gate.

Before the spies were even asleep, the woman went up to the roof and said to them, "Look, I know God has given you this land. We're all terrified of you. Everyone in this country is losing their nerve. We heard how God totally dried up the Red Sea for you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, Sihon and Og—you completely destroyed them. When we heard about it, our hearts just melted. None of us have any courage left because of you. For real, your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.

"So now, please, swear to me by God. Since I've shown you kindness, promise you'll show kindness to my family. Give me a real sign that you'll spare my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and everyone connected to them. Save us from death!"
"Our lives for yours!" the men said. "As long as you don't tell anyone about our mission. When God gives us the land, we'll treat you with loyal kindness."

So she lowered them down from a window with a rope, because her house was built right into the city wall. She told them, "Head for the hills so your pursuers don't find you. Hide out there for three days until they get back. Then you can go on your way."

The men told her, "To make this oath you made us swear legit, you have to do this: hang this red rope from the window you let us down through. Then gather your entire family—father, mother, brothers, and all your relatives—into your house with you. If anyone goes out the doors of your house into the street, their fate is on them; we're not responsible. But if a hand is laid on anyone inside the house with you, it's on us. But if you spill the beans about our business, then we're off the hook from the oath you made us swear."
She said, "Sounds like a plan," and sent them off. They left, and she immediately hung the red rope in the window.
They made their way to the hills and stayed there for three days, until the guys chasing them had returned. The pursuers had looked all over the road but didn't find them.

Then the two men started back. They came down from the hills, crossed the river, and returned to Joshua son of Nun and told him everything that had happened. They told Joshua, "For real, God has given the whole land over to us. Everyone there is literally shaking in their boots because of us."

title: God Parts the Waters, AGAIN?!
paragraphs: So, Joshua gets everyone up super early, and they all head out from Shittim. The whole crew of Israel is with him. They get to the Jordan River and set up camp, waiting to cross. Three days later, the leaders go around telling everyone the plan: 'Alright, listen up. When you see the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant, that's our cue to move out. Follow them, but don't get too close—stay back like half a mile. Seriously, keep your distance. That way, you'll see the exact path to take. This is a brand new road for us, so no messing around.'
Then Joshua tells the people, 'Get yourselves ready and be respectful. Tomorrow, God's gonna do some mind-blowing things among us.'
Joshua told the priests, 'Go ahead and pick up the Ark of the Covenant and lead the people.' So, they did just that and walked out in front of everyone.

God then says to Joshua, 'Today, I'm gonna start making you look like a big deal to all of Israel. They're gonna see for themselves that I'm with you, just like I was with Moses. Now, you tell the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant this: 'When you get to the edge of the Jordan River, just stand there on the bank.''

Then Joshua gathered the Israelites and said, 'Yo, listen up! Pay attention to what God, your God, is saying. This is how you'll know for sure that the living God is with us—he's going to totally kick out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites for you. Check it out: the Ark of the Covenant is right in front of you. And get this—the Master of the whole earth is about to cross the Jordan right before your eyes. Now, pick twelve guys from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe. When the priests carrying the Ark of God, the Master of all the earth, step into the Jordan's water, the river's flow is gonna stop. The water coming from upstream will just pile up in a huge heap.'

And that's exactly what went down. The people packed up and left their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant leading the way. The moment the priests reached the Jordan and their feet touched the water's edge (the Jordan was totally overflowing its banks because it was harvest season), the water just stopped flowing. It piled up in a massive heap way, way off at a town called Adam, which is near Zarethan. The riverbed went completely dry all the way down to the Dead Sea. So the people crossed over, right opposite Jericho.

And there they were; the priests carrying the Ark of the Covenant stood on solid, dry ground right in the middle of the Jordan while every single Israelite crossed over on dry land. The whole nation made it across without even getting their feet wet. Wild.

title: Jordan River Crossing: The Ultimate Flex
paragraphs: So, once everyone in Israel finally made it across the river, God hit up Joshua and was like, "Yo, pick twelve dudes, one from each tribe. Tell them to go to the exact spot in the middle of the Jordan where the priests are standing firm. They need to grab twelve big rocks from there, carry 'em over, and drop 'em at the spot where you guys are camping tonight."

Joshua called out the twelve guys he'd selected from the People of Israel, one from every tribe. He gave them the game plan: "Alright, head out to the middle of the Jordan and post up in front of the Ark of God, your God. Each of you needs to haul a stone onto your shoulder—one for each of the tribes of Israel. This is so you'll have something to remember this moment. Down the road, when your kids ask you, 'Yo, what's the deal with these rocks?' you'll tell them, 'The Jordan River literally stopped flowing right in front of the Ark of the Covenant when it crossed. It just stopped cold. These stones are a permanent reminder for the people of Israel.'"

The people of Israel did exactly what Joshua commanded. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan—one for each of the twelve tribes, just as God had told Joshua—carried them over to the camp, and set them down there. Joshua also set up another twelve stones right in the middle of the Jordan, at the exact spot where the priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant had stood. They're actually still there today.

The priests carrying the Ark kept standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything God had ordered Joshua to tell the people was done (which was also what Moses had told Joshua to do). The people hustled across; nobody was messing around. When every single person was safely across, they all watched as the Ark of the Covenant and the priests finally crossed over.

The soldiers from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had already crossed over in battle formation ahead of the rest of Israel, just like Moses had instructed. All in all, about forty thousand armed soldiers crossed over in God's presence, ready for battle on the plains of Jericho.
That day, God made Joshua earn serious respect in front of all of Israel. They respected him deeply, just like they had respected Moses his whole life.
Then God told Joshua, "Command the priests carrying the Ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come on up out of the Jordan."

And they did it. The priests carrying God's Ark of the Covenant came up from the middle of the Jordan. The second their feet hit dry land, the Jordan's waters started flowing again, right back to normal like nothing happened.

The people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month. They set up their camp at a place called Gilgal, just east of Jericho. Joshua then took the twelve stones they had grabbed from the Jordan and set them up as a monument at Gilgal. Then he told the Israelites, "In the future, when your kids ask their parents, 'What are these stones for?' tell them this: 'Israel crossed this Jordan river on dry ground.'

"Yeah, for real. God, your God, dried up the Jordan's waters for you until you had crossed, just like He did at the Red Sea, which he dried up for us until we crossed. This happened so that everyone on earth would know how strong God's power is, and so that you would always have a healthy respect for God."

title: The Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: So, get this: all the Amorite kings on the west side of the Jordan and the Canaanite kings on the coast heard that God literally stopped the Jordan River so the Israelites could cross. They were totally shook. Like, their courage just went *poof* and they were seriously scared of the Israelites.
Then God told Joshua, "Make some stone knives and circumcise the Israelites again." So, Joshua did just that. He made the knives and they did the circumcisions at a place they called Foreskins Hill.

Here's the deal with the circumcision. All the guys who were soldiers when they left Egypt had died in the desert on the way. The people who came out of Egypt were all circumcised, but the kids born in the desert on the journey hadn't been. The Israelites wandered in the desert for 40 years until that whole generation of soldiers who had disobeyed God died off. God promised they'd never see the awesome land He'd promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. But their kids took their place. These were the ones Joshua circumcised. They'd never had it done before on the journey.
After they finished circumcising everyone, they just chilled in the camp until they were all healed up.
God told Joshua, "Today I've rolled away the shame of Egypt." That's why they call the place The Gilgal, and they still call it that today.
The Israelites stayed camped at The Gilgal. They celebrated Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month on the plains of Jericho.

The day after Passover, they started eating the food from the land, like unleavened bread and roasted grain. And just like that, the manna stopped. As soon as they started eating the local food, there was no more manna for the Israelites. That year, they ate the crops of Canaan.
Then this happened when Joshua was near Jericho: He looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with his sword drawn. Joshua went up to him and asked, "Are you with us or with our enemies?"
He said, "Neither. I'm the commander of God's army. I just got here." Joshua immediately fell on his face and worshiped. He asked, "What are my Master's orders for his servant?"
The commander of God's army told Joshua, "Take off your sandals. The place you're standing is holy."
And Joshua did it.

title: Jericho Takedown: The Ultimate Wall Hack
paragraphs: So, Jericho was locked down tighter than a new phone on launch day because the Israelites were around. Nobody in, nobody out.

God told Joshua, “Alright, listen up. I’ve basically handed you Jericho on a silver platter—the king, the top soldiers, all of it. Here’s the game plan: You and your army are gonna march around the city once. Just one lap. Do that every day for six days. Get seven priests to carry seven special ram’s horn trumpets in front of the Ark of the Covenant. On the seventh day, you’re gonna level up and march around the city seven times, with the priests just blasting those trumpets. And then, when you hear one super long blast from the ram’s horn, everyone needs to scream their heads off. The city wall is gonna straight up collapse. Then, everyone just charges straight in.”

So Joshua, son of Nun, got the priests together and was like, “Okay, grab the Ark of the Covenant. And seven of you priests, you get the seven ram’s horn trumpets and lead the way in front of God’s Ark.”
Then he told the people, “Let’s go! Start marching around the city. The armed guards will go in front of God’s Ark.”

And just like that, it happened. Joshua gave the word, and the people were on the move. Seven priests with their seven ram’s horn trumpets went out ahead of God. They were blowing the trumpets, leading God’s Ark of the Covenant. The armed guard marched in front of the trumpet-playing priests, and the rear guard marched behind the Ark, all while the trumpets were blasting.
Joshua had given the people one major rule: “Don’t shout. Seriously, don’t even talk. Not a whisper. Wait until I give the signal and say ‘Shout!’—then you can go wild.”

He had the Ark of God do a lap around the city. It circled once, then they all went back to camp and crashed for the night. Joshua was up bright and early the next morning, and the priests picked up the Ark of God again. The seven priests with the seven ram’s horn trumpets marched in front of God’s Ark, marching and blowing their trumpets, with the armed guard in front and the rear guard behind. Marching and trumpets, that was the whole scene!
On the second day, they did the same thing—circled the city once and went back to camp. They kept this up for six days straight.

When the seventh day rolled around, they got up at dawn and marched around the city just like before, but this time they did it seven times. Yep, seven laps on day seven. On the seventh time around, the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua gave the signal to the people, “SHOUT! God has given you the city! The city and everything in it is totally off-limits for God, a holy offering.
“Except for Rahab the prostitute—she gets to live, her and everyone in her house. Why? Because she hid the spies we sent.

“And for you guys, be super careful in this off-limits city. Don’t get greedy and take anything that’s cursed. You’ll bring that same curse on the whole camp of Israel and cause a ton of trouble for everyone. All the silver and gold, all the bronze and iron stuff, that’s all holy to God. It goes straight into God’s treasury.”
The priests blew the trumpets.
When the people heard that trumpet blast, they let out this insane roar. The wall collapsed instantly. The people stormed straight into the city and took it.
They dedicated everything in the city to God by destroying it—men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.

Joshua told the two guys who had spied on the land, “Go to the prostitute’s house and get her and her family out, just like you promised.” So the young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, mother, brothers—her whole crew. They got the entire family out and set them up in a safe spot outside the Israelite camp. Then they burned the whole city and everything in it to the ground. The only things they saved were the gold, silver, and the bronze and iron items—all that went into the treasury of God’s house.

But Joshua let Rahab the prostitute live—her and her father’s family and everyone connected to her. She’s actually still living in Israel today, all because she hid the agents Joshua sent to spy on Jericho.
Then Joshua made a super serious vow right then and there:
Cursed by God is the person who tries to rebuild this city, Jericho. He’ll lay the foundation with his firstborn son, and he’ll set up the gates with his youngest son.
God was with Joshua, for real. He got famous all over the country.

title: One Guy's Mistake Wrecked the Whole Battle
paragraphs: But then the Israelites totally broke the rules. This guy named Achan—son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah—from the tribe of Judah, took some of the stuff that was supposed to be destroyed under the holy curse. And God got really mad at the people of Israel.
Joshua sent some men from Jericho to a town called Ai, which is near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He told them, 'Go up and scout out the land.' So the men went and spied on Ai.
They came back to Joshua and said, 'Don't send the whole army. Just two or three thousand men will be enough to take down Ai. No need to wear everyone out; there aren't even that many people there.'

So about three thousand men went up, but they ended up getting chased away by the men of Ai! The guys from Ai killed about thirty-six of them and chased them from the city gate all the way to the quarries, killing them on the way down. The people's courage just melted away; they were totally demoralized.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell face down on the ground in front of the Ark of God. He and the elders of Israel stayed there until evening, throwing dirt on their heads.

Joshua cried out, 'Oh, man... Lord GOD, why did you even bring us across the Jordan River? Just to hand us over to the Amorites to be destroyed? We should have just stayed on the other side of the Jordan! Oh, Lord, what can I even say now that Israel has run away from its enemies? When the Canaanites and everyone else living here hears about this, they'll surround us and wipe us out. And then what about your great name?'

God said to Joshua, 'Get up! Why are you lying on your face like that? Israel has sinned. They've broken the covenant I commanded them. They've taken some of the cursed things—they stole them, lied about it, and hid them with their own stuff. That's why the Israelites can't stand up to their enemies; they've become cursed themselves. I won't be with you anymore unless you get rid of the cursed things from among you.'

'So get up and purify the people. Tell them: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is something cursed among you, Israel. You won't be able to face your enemies until you remove it.'

'In the morning, you'll come forward by your tribes. The tribe the LORD chooses will come forward by clans, the clan the LORD chooses will come forward by families, and the family the LORD chooses will come forward man by man. The one who is caught with the cursed things will be burned with fire, along with everything he has, because he has broken the LORD's covenant and has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.'

Joshua got up early the next morning and had Israel come forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was chosen. Then he had the clans of Judah come forward, and the Zerahites were chosen. He had the Zerahite clan come forward by families, and Zabdi's family was chosen. He had the family members come forward one by one, and Achan son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Then Joshua said to Achan, 'My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him praise. Tell me what you have done. Don't hide it from me.'

Achan replied, 'It's true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did: When I saw a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels in the plunder, I wanted them so I took them. They're hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.'

So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. And there it was, hidden in his tent with the silver underneath. They took the items from the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and laid them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, together with all of Israel, took Achan, the silver, the robe, the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and everything he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor (which means 'Trouble').

Joshua said, 'Why have you brought this trouble on us? The LORD will bring trouble on you today.' Then all of Israel stoned him, and after that, they burned them with fire and stoned them. They piled a huge heap of stones over him that is still there today. Then the LORD turned from his fierce anger. That's why that place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.

title: The Ultimate Comeback: How We Faked a Retreat and Conquered Ai
paragraphs: God told Joshua, "Yo, don't be scared or even hesitate for a second. Grab your whole squad and head back to Ai. I'm handing you the king of Ai on a silver platter—his crew, his city, the whole deal.
"You're gonna do to Ai and its king exactly what you did to Jericho and its king. But this time, you can take all their stuff and animals. Go wild. Set up a surprise attack behind the city."

So Joshua and his whole army got ready to roll out to Ai. He picked thirty thousand of his toughest, most experienced fighters and sent them out at night with these instructions: "Alright, listen up. I need you to sneak behind the city and hide. Get as close as you can without being seen, and stay ready. Me and my guys will go straight for the city. When they come out to fight us like last time, we're gonna pretend to be scared and run away. They'll chase us and leave the city wide open. They'll be thinking, 'Ha, they're running away again!' That's when you guys jump out of your hiding spot and take over the city. God's got your back and will basically hand you the city. Once you're in, burn it all down. God's orders. Now go. I've given you your mission."
So Joshua sent them out. They set up their ambush and waited between Bethel and Ai, to the west. Joshua stayed with the rest of the people that night.

Joshua was up at the crack of dawn, got his army together, and with the leaders of Israel, they all marched to Ai. The whole army, all the soldiers, marched until they could see the city and set up camp on the north side. There was a valley separating them from Ai. He had taken about five thousand men and put them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city. They were all in position, the main army to the north and the ambush to the west. Joshua spent that night in the valley.

So, when the king of Ai saw them, he and his men didn't waste any time. They rushed out at sunrise to fight Israel at a spot overlooking the Arabah. The king had no idea there was an ambush waiting for him behind the city.

Joshua and all of Israel pretended to get beaten and ran towards the wilderness. The entire city was called out to chase them. They went after Joshua and got lured away from their city. Not a single person was left in Ai or Bethel; everyone was out chasing Israel. They left the city completely undefended.

Then God said to Joshua, "Point your javelin toward Ai—I'm giving it to you." So Joshua pointed his javelin toward Ai. As soon as he gave the signal, the guys in ambush jumped up, ran into the city, captured it, and immediately set it on fire.

The men of Ai looked back and, oh man, saw their city going up in smoke. They were totally trapped with nowhere to run. The army that had been running away to the wilderness suddenly turned around—Joshua and all of Israel saw that the ambush had worked and the city was burning, so they turned back and attacked the men of Ai.

Then the ambush squad came pouring out of the city. The men of Ai were caught in the middle with Israelites on both sides—it was a total slaughter. Not a single one of them survived. Except for the king of Ai; they captured him alive and brought him to Joshua.

When it was all over, Israel had killed every last person from Ai, both in the fields and in the wilderness where they had chased them. Once the killing was done, the Israelites went back to Ai and finished the job. The total number of people who died that day was twelve thousand, everyone in Ai.

Joshua didn't lower his javelin until every single person in Ai was completely wiped out as a sacred offering. But Israel did get to take the animals and all the loot from the city, just like God had told Joshua they could.

Joshua burned Ai to the ground. It became a permanent pile of ruins, a total wasteland—you can still see it today. He hanged the king of Ai on a tree and left him there until evening. When the sun went down, Joshua ordered them to take the body down. They threw it at the city entrance and piled a huge mound of rocks over it—you can still see that too.

Then Joshua built an altar to the God of Israel on Mount Ebal. He built it exactly as Moses, God's servant, had instructed the Israelites, as written in the Book of the Law of Moses—an altar made of natural, uncut stones. On it, they presented burnt offerings and peace offerings to God. He also wrote a copy of the Law of Moses on the stones right there in front of all the Israelites.

All of Israel was there—foreigners and citizens alike—with their elders, officials, and judges. They stood on opposite sides of the Ark of the Covenant, facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half of them stood in front of Mount Gerizim and the other half in front of Mount Ebal to bless the people of Israel, just as Moses, the servant of God, had commanded.

After that, Joshua read every single word from the Book of the Law—the blessings and the curses, everything. There wasn't a single word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua didn't read to the entire assembly—men, women, children, and the foreigners who were traveling with them.

title: The Great Gibeonite Deception
paragraphs: So, all the kings west of the Jordan River—in the hills, the foothills, and along the Mediterranean coast up to Lebanon—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Girgashites, and Jebusites, all heard the news. They decided to team up and fight Joshua and Israel as one big army.

But the people from Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai and came up with a wild plan. They pretended to be travelers from a faraway land. They loaded up their donkeys with old, patched-up sacks and cracked wineskins. They wore worn-out sandals and raggedy clothes, and their food was just dry, moldy bread crumbs. They went to Joshua at Gilgal and said to the men of Israel, “We’ve come from a super distant country. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
The Israelites were skeptical, though. They said to these Hivites, “Hold on, how do we know you’re not our neighbors? If you are, we can’t make a treaty with you.”
They replied to Joshua, “We’ll be your servants.”
Joshua was like, “Who are you, really? And where are you from?”

They said, “Oh, we’re from a country that’s, like, really, really far away. Your servants came because we heard about your God and all the amazing things he did in Egypt! And we heard about the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth! Our leaders and everyone in our country told us, ‘Pack some food for a long trip and go meet them. Tell them, ‘We’re your servants; make a treaty with us.’

“Check out this bread. It was warm when we packed it, but now it’s all hard and moldy. And these wineskins were brand new, but now they’re all cracked and patched up. Our clothes and sandals are totally wrecked from the super long journey.”
The men of Israel looked at their stuff and bought their story. But they didn’t even think to ask God about it.
So Joshua made peace with them and signed a treaty to let them live. The leaders of the community swore an oath to seal the deal.

But then, just three days after they made the treaty, the Israelites found out that the Gibeonites were actually their next-door neighbors! The Israelites packed up and, three days later, they arrived at their towns: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim. But the Israelites didn’t attack them because their leaders had made a promise to them in front of the God of Israel. The whole community was seriously mad at their leaders, though.

The leaders all agreed on what to do. They told the people, “We made a promise to them in front of the God of Israel. We can’t touch them now. But here’s what we’ll do: we’ll let them live so we don’t get in trouble for breaking our promise.” Then the leaders added, “We’ll let them live, but they’ll have to be our woodcutters and water carriers for the whole community.”
And that’s what happened. The leaders kept their promise.

But Joshua called the Gibeonites and said, “Why did you lie to us? You said you lived super far away, but you’re literally our neighbors! Because of that, you’re cursed. From now on, you’ll be doing all the hard labor—cutting wood and carrying water for the house of my God.”

They answered Joshua, “Look, we heard that your God commanded his servant Moses to give you this whole land and to destroy everyone living in it. We were terrified of you, and that’s why we did this. So, here we are. We’re at your mercy. Do whatever you think is right.”

And that’s what Joshua did. He saved them from being killed by the Israelites. But he made them woodcutters and water carriers for the community and for the Altar of God, wherever God would choose it to be. And they still are to this day.

title: Sun FREEZES, Kings DEFEATED! Joshua's Most EPIC Battle
paragraphs: So, it didn't take long for King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem to get the news. He heard that Joshua had captured Ai, totally destroying it and its king, just like he'd done to Jericho. He also found out that the people of Gibeon had made a peace deal with Israel and were now living right next to them. This freaked him and his people out. Gibeon was a major city, as big as any royal city and even bigger than Ai, and all its guys were legit warriors.

So Adoni-Zedek, the king of Jerusalem, sent messages to King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. He was like, 'Yo, come help me out. Let's go attack Gibeon. They've teamed up with Joshua and the Israelites.'
So the five Amorite kings—from Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—got their armies together and marched out to attack Gibeon.

The guys from Gibeon quickly sent a message to Joshua, who was camped at Gilgal: 'Don't bail on us now! Get up here fast! Save us! Help! All the Amorite kings from the hill country have ganged up on us.'

So Joshua took off from Gilgal with his whole army, including all his toughest soldiers. God told him, 'Don't even worry about them. I've already handed them to you. Not a single one of them will be able to stand against you.'

Joshua marched all night from Gilgal and caught them completely by surprise. God threw the enemy into total chaos, and Israel won a huge victory at Gibeon. They chased them down the road to Beth Horon, fighting them all the way to Azekah and Makkedah. As the enemy was running from the Israelites down the slope from Beth Horon, God started dropping massive hailstones on them from the sky, all the way to Azekah. More of them died from the hail than from the Israelites' swords. Wild.
The day God handed the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua prayed to God in front of all the Israelites:
'Sun, stand still over Gibeon! Moon, stop over the Valley of Aijalon!' And the sun actually stopped, and the moon stood still, until the nation of Israel had defeated its enemies.

(This is actually written down in the Book of Jashar, for real.) The sun stopped right in the middle of the sky and just stayed there for a whole day. There has never been a day like it before or since, when God took orders from a human. God was really fighting for Israel that day.
Then Joshua and all the Israelites with him went back to their camp at Gilgal.
Meanwhile, the five kings had run off and were hiding in a cave at Makkedah. Someone told Joshua, 'Hey, we found the five kings hiding in the cave at Makkedah.'

Joshua said, 'Roll some big rocks over the entrance of the cave and post some guards there. But don't you guys just hang around. Go after your enemies. Cut them off before they can get back to their cities. God has given them to you.'

So Joshua and the Israelites finished them off in a massive slaughter. Only a few survivors managed to escape to their fortified cities. Then the whole army came back to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and no one in Israel had a single bad thing to say.
Then Joshua said, 'Open up the cave and bring those five kings to me.'
So they did. They brought the five kings out of the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
When they had brought all the kings to Joshua, he called over all the men of Israel and told the army commanders who had been with him, 'Come here. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.'
So they came forward and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua told them, 'Don't be scared. Don't be timid. Be strong and courageous. This is what God is going to do to all the enemies you fight against.'

Then Joshua struck and killed the kings. He had them hung on five trees, and they were left there until evening. At sunset, Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. They sealed the entrance of the cave with large stones, and they're still there to this day.
That same day, Joshua captured Makkedah and completely destroyed it, including its king. He left no survivors. He did the same thing to the king of Makkedah that he had done to the king of Jericho.

Then Joshua and all Israel with him went from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it. God also gave Libnah to Israel. They captured the city and its king and killed everyone. No survivors. They did the same thing to the king of Libnah as they had to the king of Jericho.

Joshua and all Israel with him then moved from Libnah to Lachish, set up camp nearby, and attacked it. God gave Lachish to Israel, and they took it on the second day. They killed everyone in it, just as they had done to Libnah.
Then King Horam of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua defeated him and his army until there were no survivors left.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped and attacked it. They captured it that day and killed everyone, just like they had done at Lachish.

Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it. They captured it and killed its king, all its villages, and everyone in them. No survivors, just like at Eglon. They completely destroyed the city and everyone in it.

Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned toward Debir and attacked it. He captured it, its king, and all its villages. They killed everyone and completely destroyed everything. No survivors. They did to Debir and its king what they had done to Hebron, and to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua conquered the whole land: the hill country, the Negev, the western foothills, and the mountain slopes. He defeated all their kings and left no survivors. He completely destroyed everything that breathed, just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded. Joshua's conquest went from Kadesh Barnea all the way to Gaza, and included the whole region of Goshen up to Gibeon. Joshua captured all these kings and their lands in one single campaign because the LORD, the God of Israel, was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua and all the Israelites with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.

title: The Final Boss Battle: Northern Alliance
paragraphs: Alright, so when King Jabin of Hazor got the news about everything, he immediately sent messages out. He hit up Jobab, king of Madon, the king of Shimron, the king of Acshaph, and all the kings up in the northern mountains. He also reached out to the kings in the valley south of Kinnereth, those in the western foothills and Naphoth Dor, the Canaanites from both east and west, plus the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the hill country. And, of course, the Hivites living below Mount Hermon near Mizpah.

They all showed up, bringing their entire armies. It was a huge force, seriously, like the number of grains of sand on a beach. And that's not even counting all the horses and chariots. All these kings linked up and camped together at the Waters of Merom, getting ready to throw down with Israel.

But God told Joshua, "Yo, don't even worry about them. By this time tomorrow, I'm gonna hand them all over to Israel, completely defeated. You're going to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots."

So Joshua and his whole army launched a surprise attack, catching them off guard at the Waters of Merom. God gave Israel the victory. They crushed them and chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and over to the Valley of Mizpah in the east. There were zero survivors. Joshua did exactly what God told him to do: he disabled their horses and torched their chariots.

After that, Joshua went back and conquered Hazor, killing its king. Back in the day, Hazor was the leader of all these kingdoms. They wiped out every single person there, fulfilling the holy curse—not a single person was left breathing. Then, he burned Hazor to the ground.

Joshua captured all the royal cities and their kings, and he completely destroyed them as a holy curse, just like Moses, God's servant, had commanded. However, Israel didn't burn down the cities built on mounds, with the one exception of Hazor—Joshua made sure that one was burned. The Israelites took all the loot and cattle from these towns for themselves. But they killed all the people, a total wipeout. They left nothing human alive.
It was just like God had commanded his servant Moses. Moses passed the command to Joshua, and Joshua saw it through. He didn't leave a single thing unfinished that God had ordered Moses to do.

So Joshua took over the entire land: the mountains, the southern desert, all of Goshen, the foothills, the valley, and the mountains of Israel with their foothills. He conquered from Mount Halak, which overlooks Seir, all the way to Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon, in the shadow of Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and executed them. Joshua was at war with these kings for a long time. Not a single town made a peace treaty with the Israelites, except for the Hivites in Gibeon. Israel had to fight for and conquer all the rest. It was actually God's plan for them to be stubborn and fight Israel, so they could be completely destroyed under the holy curse, without any mercy, just as God had commanded Moses.

During that time, Joshua also went to get rid of the Anakim from the hill country—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and from the mountains of Judah and Israel. Joshua put them and their cities under the holy curse. No Anakim were left in the land of Israel, except for a few who remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took the whole region, doing everything exactly as God had told Moses. Then he divided up the land as an inheritance for the tribes of Israel.
And finally, Israel had a break from war.

title: Israel's Victory Lap: All The Kings They Beat
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the rundown of all the kings the Israelites totally wrecked east of the Jordan River. They took over their land from the Arnon Gorge all the way to Mount Hermon, including the whole eastern side of the Arabah Valley.

First up, there was this dude Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. His kingdom was huge, stretching from Aroer by the Arnon Gorge, through the middle of the gorge, over half of Gilead, all the way to the Jabbok River gorge, which was the border with the Ammonites. He also controlled the eastern Arabah Valley, from the Sea of Kinnereth down to the Dead Sea, and then east towards Beth Jeshimoth and south to the slopes of Pisgah. Man had a lot of land.

Then there was Og, the king of Bashan. This guy was one of the last of the Rephaim giants, for real. He ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei, and his territory covered everything from Mount Hermon and Salecah, all of Bashan, right up to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites—which was the other half of Gilead—and then to the border of King Sihon's land.

So yeah, Moses, God's main man, and the Israelites rolled in and defeated both of them. Then Moses, being the solid leader he was, gave all that land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of the tribe of Manasseh as their new home.

And on the other side, west of the Jordan, Joshua and the Israelites defeated a whole bunch of other kings. They took the land from Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon all the way south to Mount Halak, which looms over Seir. Joshua then divided up this land for the tribes of Israel to own, each getting their own section. This included the mountains, the western foothills, the Arabah Valley, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev desert. Basically, all the places where the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites used to live. The kings they defeated were:

The king of Jericho, one. The king of Ai (near Bethel), one. The king of Jerusalem, one. The king of Hebron, one. The king of Jarmuth, one. The king of Lachish, one. The king of Eglon, one. The king of Gezer, one. The king of Debir, one. The king of Geder, one. The king of Hormah, one. The king of Arad, one. The king of Libnah, one. The king of Adullam, one. The king of Makkedah, one. The king of Bethel, one. The king of Tappuah, one. The king of Hepher, one. The king of Aphek, one. The king of Lasharon, one. The king of Madon, one. The king of Hazor, one. The king of Shimron Meron, one. The king of Acshaph, one. The king of Taanach, one. The king of Megiddo, one. The king of Kedesh, one. The king of Jokneam in Carmel, one. The king of Dor (Naphoth Dor), one. The king of Goyim in Gilgal, one. The king of Tirzah, one.
That's a grand total of thirty-one kings. For real.

title: God's To-Do List for Joshua
paragraphs: So Joshua was getting on in years, like, for real old. God hit him up and said, 'Bro, you've lived a good, long life, but there's still a ton of land we gotta take over. This is the land that's left:

all the Philistine and Geshurite areas; the land from the Shihor River east of Egypt all the way to Ekron's border up north, which is Canaanite turf (there were five big-shot Philistine bosses in Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron); also the Avvim from the south; all the Canaanite land from Arah (which belonged to the Sidonians) to Aphek at the Amorite border; the country of the Gebalites; all of Lebanon to the east from Baal Gad in the shadow of Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath; everyone living in the mountains, from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim; all the Sidonians.

'I'll personally kick them out for the Israelites. All you gotta do is divide up this land for Israel as their inheritance, just like I told you. So get on it now: give out this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.'
The other half-tribe of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had already gotten their inheritance from Moses on the east side of the Jordan. Moses, God's servant, gave it to them.

Their land went from Aroer at the edge of the Arnon Gorge and the city in the middle of the valley, and it included the whole tableland of Medeba as far as Dibon, and all the towns of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon, all the way to the Ammonite border. It also had Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah—the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who was king in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaim giants. Moses had crushed them and taken their land. But the Israelites never actually kicked out the Geshurites and Maacathites—they're still living in Israel to this day.
Levi was the only tribe that didn't get an inheritance. The offerings made to God, the God of Israel, were their inheritance, just like he told them.
This is what Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan:
the land from Aroer at the edge of the Arnon Gorge and the town in the middle of the valley, including the tableland around Medeba;

Heshbon on the tableland with all its towns (Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar on Valley Mountain, Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth Jeshimoth);

and all the cities of the tableland, the whole kingdom of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled at Heshbon. Moses had taken him down along with the Midianite princes: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were all Sihon's puppets living in that country. (On top of those killed in the fighting, the Israelites also took out Balaam son of Beor, the fortune-teller.)
The border for the Reubenites was the bank of the Jordan River. This was the inheritance for the Reubenites, their villages and cities, according to their clans.
To the tribe of Gad, clan by clan, Moses gave:
the area of Jazer and all the towns of Gilead and half the Ammonite country as far as Aroer near Rabbah;
the land from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the Debir region;
in the valley: Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon (the east side of the Jordan, north to the end of the Sea of Kinnereth).
This was the inheritance for the Gadites, their cities and villages, clan by clan.
To the half-tribe of Manasseh, clan by clan, Moses gave:
the land stretching out from Mahanaim;
all of Bashan, which is the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the settlements of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns in total.
Half of Gilead with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan, belong to the descendants of Makir, a son of Manasseh (so, the half-tribe of the children of Makir) for their clans.

So yeah, that's the inheritance Moses handed out when he was on the plains of Moab across the Jordan, east of Jericho. But Moses didn't give any inheritance to the tribe of Levi. God, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just like he told them.

title: Caleb's Comeback: 85 & Still a Beast
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the breakdown of the land the Israelites got in Canaan. The priest Eleazar, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the family clans were in charge of handing it out.

They basically drew lots for the nine and a half tribes to decide who got what, just like God had told Moses to do. Moses had already sorted out the other two and a half tribes with land east of the Jordan River. The Levites, though, didn't get a piece of the land pie like the others. That's because Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, had become their own tribes. So, the Levites didn't get a big chunk of land, but they did get cities to live in with some pasture for their animals.
So, the Israelites did exactly what God had commanded Moses, and they divided up the land.

Then, the guys from the tribe of Judah went to see Joshua at Gilgal. Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, stepped up and said, “Yo, you remember what God said to Moses, the man of God, about you and me way back at Kadesh Barnea, right? I was forty when Moses, God's servant, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to check out the land. I came back and gave a totally honest report, for real.

The other guys who went with me freaked everyone out and made them scared, but I went all in and trusted God, my God, completely. So that day, Moses made a serious promise. He said, ‘The land you walked on will be your inheritance forever, for you and your kids, because you followed God with your whole heart.’

So look at me now. God kept his promise and has kept me alive. It’s been 45 years since God said that to Moses, all those years the Israelites were wandering in the desert. And here I am, 85 years old! But I’m just as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. I’m ready to fight, to go out and come back, just like I was back then. So give me that hill country God promised me on that day. You heard the report yourself—the Anakim giants were there with their huge, fortified cities. But if God is with me, I’ll drive them out, just like He said.”

Joshua was impressed and gave Caleb his blessing. He gave him the city of Hebron as his inheritance. And that’s why Hebron still belongs to the descendants of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite today—because he was all-in for God, the God of Israel.
Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba. It was named after Arba, who was like the most legendary guy among the Anakim.
And with that, the land finally had a break from all the fighting.

title: Judah's Land Is HUGE (And Caleb's Daughter Is a Genius)
paragraphs: Alright, so the land assigned to the tribe of Judah, broken down by their family groups, stretched all the way south to the border of Edom, hitting the Zin wilderness at the very bottom.

The southern border started from the tip of the Salt Sea, just south of a spot called The Tongue. It went south from Scorpions Pass, looped around Zin, and passed just south of Kadesh Barnea. Then it went past Hezron, up to Addar, and curved around to Karka. From there, it continued to Azmon, came out at the Brook of Egypt, and finished at the Sea. That was their whole southern property line.
The eastern border was just the Salt Sea, all the way up to where the Jordan River empties into it.

The northern border kicked off at the shallow part of the Sea where the Jordan ends. It went up to Beth Hoglah, wrapped around the north of Beth Arabah, and went to the Stone of Bohan (Reuben's son). From there, the line went up to Debir from the Valley of Trouble and then turned north towards Gilgal, which is across from Red Pass, just south of the canyon. The border then followed the En Shemesh stream and ended at En Rogel. It continued along the Valley of Ben Hinnom on the south side of the Jebusite ridge (which is Jerusalem). It climbed to the top of the mountain across from Hinnom Valley on the west, at the north end of Rephaim Valley. The border then made a turn at the mountaintop to the spring of Nephtoah, followed the valley to Mount Ephron, turned towards Baalah (that's Kiriath Jearim), and then took another turn west of Baalah to Mount Seir. It curved around the north side of Mount Jearim (aka Kesalon), went down to Beth Shemesh, and crossed over to Timnah. The border then headed north to the ridge of Ekron, turned toward Shikkeron, passed Mount Baalah, and came out at Jabneel. The whole thing ended at the Sea.
The western border was simply the coastline of the Great Sea.
So, that's the complete boundary for all the clans of the tribe of Judah.

As a side note, Joshua gave Caleb, son of Jephunneh, his own piece of land among the people of Judah, just like God told him to. He got Kiriath Arba, which is now called Hebron. Arba was the original ancestor of the giant-like Anakim.

Caleb kicked out the three big Anakim dudes from Hebron: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, who were all descendants of Anak. After that, he went up to fight the people of Debir. Debir's old name was Kiriath Sepher.

Caleb made a deal: 'Whoever attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher, I'll give them my daughter Acsah as a wife.' Othniel, son of Kenaz (Caleb's brother), was the one who took it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Acsah to marry.

When she got there, she convinced Othniel to ask her dad for some farmland. As she was getting off her donkey, Caleb asked her, 'What's up? What do you need?' She said, 'Can you give me a real wedding present? You've given me land in the middle of nowhere; now give me some water sources!' So he gave her both the upper and the lower pools. Talk about a good dad.
This was the inheritance for the tribe of Judah, clan by clan.
The towns in the south of Judah's tribe, down in the Negev desert near the Edom border, were:

Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah, Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan, Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (which is Hazor), Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet, Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah, Baalah, Iim, Ezem, Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon—making a total of twenty-nine towns plus their surrounding villages.

In the Shephelah (the foothills to the west), they had: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, and Gederah (or Gederothaim)—that's fourteen towns with their villages. Then Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad, Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish, Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah—another sixteen towns with their villages. And Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Aczib, and Mareshah—nine towns with their villages. Ekron with its towns and villages; from Ekron west to the sea, everything that bordered Ashdod and its villages; Ashdod with its towns and villages; Gaza with its towns and villages, all the way to the Brook of Egypt. The Great Sea was the western border.

In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that's Debir), Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven towns and their villages. Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath Arba (aka Hebron), and Zior—nine towns and their villages. Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah—ten towns and their villages. Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor, Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon—six towns and their villages. Kiriath Baal (which is Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah—two towns and their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi—six towns and their villages.

But the people of Judah just couldn't kick out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites stayed right where they were, living with the people of Judah. And they're actually still living there in Jerusalem to this day.

title: Ephraim's Crew Gets Their Land!
paragraphs: Alright, so the land for Joseph's descendants started from the Jordan River near Jericho, east of the Jericho spring, and went up north through the desert mountains to Bethel. From Bethel (which is also called Luz), it continued to the Arkite territory in Ataroth. Then, it went down west to the Japhletite area, reaching Lower Beth Horon and then Gezer, finally ending at the Mediterranean Sea.
This was the chunk of land that Joseph's two crews, Manasseh and Ephraim, inherited.
The territory for Ephraim's clans was marked out like this:

Their inheritance boundary started at Ataroth Addar in the east and went to Upper Beth Horon, then continued west until it hit the Sea. From Micmethath in the north, the border curved east to Taanath Shiloh and kept going east to Janoah. From Janoah, the border dropped down to Ataroth and Naarah, grazed Jericho, and came out at the Jordan River. The border then went west from Tappuah to the Kanah Brook and ended at the Sea. That was the inheritance for the tribe of Ephraim, clan by clan, and it even included some towns that were technically in Manasseh's territory—all those towns and their villages.

But here's the thing, they didn't actually kick out the Canaanites who were living in Gezer. So, to this day, Canaanites are still living there among the Ephraimites, but they're basically forced to do all the hard labor.

title: Don't Lowball Us, We Got Heirs!
paragraphs: Alright, so here's the breakdown of the land that went to the tribe of Manasseh, who was Joseph's firstborn son. Quick backstory: Gilead and Bashan were already given to Makir, Manasseh's oldest and a total beast in battle. So, the rest of the land was divided up among the other clans of Manasseh: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the main family lines of Manasseh, Joseph's son.

Now, check this out. There was this guy, Zelophehad—son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh—who had no sons—only five daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. These girls were seriously brave. They marched right up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and all the leaders and said, 'Yo, God told Moses that we should get an inheritance just like our male relatives.' And Joshua, being a real one, did exactly what God commanded and gave them their own land right there with their uncles.

So, Manasseh's territory was split into ten shares, plus the lands of Gilead and Bashan on the other side of the Jordan. This happened because Manasseh's daughters got their inheritance right alongside his sons, which was a pretty big deal back then. The land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.

The border for Manasseh's land started at Asher and went all the way to Micmethath, which is across from Shechem. From there, it went south to where the people of En Tappuah lived. The area of Tappuah was Manasseh's, but the actual town of Tappuah on the border belonged to the tribe of Ephraim. The border then went down to the Kanah Brook. The cities in that area were technically Ephraim's, even though they were inside Manasseh's territory. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the brook and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. So, the land south of the brook was Ephraim's, the land to the north was Manasseh's, the sea was their western border, and they bordered Asher to the north and Issachar to the east.

On top of all that, Manasseh also got some towns inside Issachar and Asher's territory: Beth Shan, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo, along with all their surrounding villages. The third one in that list is Naphoth.

But here's the thing, the people of Manasseh couldn't actually kick the Canaanites out of these towns. The Canaanites just wouldn't leave. It was only later, when the Israelites got a lot stronger, that they made the Canaanites their forced laborers. But they never fully got rid of them.

Then, the people of Joseph—which includes both Ephraim and Manasseh—came to Joshua and were like, 'Hey, why did you only give us one piece of land? There are a ton of us, and God has blessed us like crazy, so we're growing!'

Joshua's response was basically, 'Okay, if there are so many of you and the hill country of Ephraim is too small, then go up into the forest in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim and clear out some space for yourselves.'

But the Joseph crew wasn't having it. They said, 'The hill country isn't enough for us, and all the Canaanites living down in the plains have iron chariots, which is some next-level tech. They're in Beth Shan and the Jezreel Valley, and we can't beat that.'

Joshua laid it down for the house of Joseph (both Ephraim and Manasseh): 'You're right, there are a lot of you, and you're super strong. One share isn't enough. So you also get the hill country. Yeah, it's all forest right now, but you're going to clear it and own it from end to end. And don't even trip about the Canaanites. Even with their iron chariots and their power, they won't stand a chance against you. You got this.'

title: Time to Claim Your Land, No More Chillin'!
paragraphs: Alright, so the entire crew of Israelites gathered at Shiloh. They set up the sacred Tent of Meeting right there.
The land was pretty much under their control, but plot twist: there were still seven Israelite tribes that hadn't gotten their own piece of land yet.

Joshua stepped up and said to the people, "Yo, for real, how long are you guys gonna just chill and put off claiming the land that God, the God of your ancestors, has given you? Pick three dudes from each tribe so I can send them on a mission. They're gonna survey the land, map it out to show what each tribe gets, and then report back to me. They'll divide it into seven parts. Judah will stay in its area in the south, and the house of Joseph will keep their spot in the north.
"You guys are in charge of making a map with seven sections. Bring it to me, and I'll cast lots for you here in front of our God.

"Just a heads-up, the Levites don't get a piece of the land because their inheritance is serving as God's priests. And you know Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh already got their land on the east side of the Jordan, which Moses, God's servant, gave them."

So the chosen guys got ready to leave. As they were heading out to survey the land, Joshua gave them their orders: "Go. Check out the land and map it. Then come back to me, and I'll cast lots for you here at Shiloh in God's presence."
So the men took off. They went through the whole area and drew a map of the territory, town by town, on a scroll. Then they came back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them there in Shiloh, right in front of God. And that's how Joshua divided up the land for the People of Israel, giving each tribe their share.
The first lot was for the tribe of Benjamin and its clans. The territory they got was located between the people of Judah and the people of Joseph.

Their northern border started at the Jordan River, went up the ridge north of Jericho, and then west into the hill country to the wilderness of Beth Aven. From there, the border went around to Luz (which is Bethel) on its southern ridge, and then down from Ataroth Addar to the mountain south of Lower Beth Horon.

On the west side, the border made a turn and went south from the mountain south of Beth Horon, ending at Kiriath Baal (that's Kiriath Jearim), a town belonging to the people of Judah. That was the west side.

The southern border started at the edge of Kiriath Jearim on the west, ran west to the Waters of Nephtoah spring. Then it went down to the base of the mountain facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom (north of the Valley of Rephaim), continued down through the Hinnom Valley just south of the Jebusite ridge, and went on to En Rogel. From there, it curved north to En Shemesh and Geliloth, across from the Red Pass (Adummim), down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben, kept going north along the side of Beth Arabah, and then dropped down to the Arabah. It then followed the slope of Beth Hoglah to the north and ended at the northern tip of the Salt Sea—where the Jordan River flows in. That was the southern border.
The Jordan River formed the eastern border.
This was the inheritance for the clans of Benjamin, with these borders all around.
The towns for the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan, were:

Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz, Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Kephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba—a total of twelve towns with their villages. Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city (which is Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath Jearim—a total of fourteen cities with their villages.
This was the inheritance for Benjamin, according to its clans.

title: The Great Land Giveaway Finale!
paragraphs: The second lot was for the tribe of Simeon, clan by clan. Their inheritance was actually located within the territory of Judah. They received Beersheba (also known as Sheba), Moladah, Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem, Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah, Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen—a total of thirteen towns and their surrounding villages. They also got Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four towns with their villages—plus all the villages around these towns as far as Baalath Beer, which is the Ramah of the Negev.

This was the inheritance for the tribe of Simeon according to their clans. The reason Simeon's inheritance came from Judah's share was that Judah's portion was way bigger than they needed. So, the people of Simeon got their land from within Judah's territory.

The third lot went to Zebulun, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance went all the way to Sarid. From there, it ran west to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and then continued to the brook opposite Jokneam. Going the other way from Sarid, the border went east, following the sunrise to the border of Kisloth Tabor, then on to Daberath and up to Japhia. It kept going east to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin, came out at Rimmon, and curved toward Neah. There, the border looped north to Hannathon and ended in the Valley of Iphtah El. This area included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities with their villages.
This is the inheritance the people of Zebulun received for their clans—these towns and their villages.

The fourth lot was for the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan. Their territory included Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez. The boundary touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh, and it ended at the Jordan River—sixteen towns and their villages in total.
These towns with their villages were the inheritance for the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan.

The fifth lot went to the tribe of Asher, clan by clan. Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Acshaph, Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. The western border touched Carmel and Shihor Libnath, then turned east toward Beth Dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah El, and went north to Beth Emek and Neiel, passing Cabul on the left. It continued to Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, all the way to the major city of Sidon. The border then circled back toward Ramah, extended to the fortress city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea in the region of Aczib, Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two towns and their villages.
These towns and villages were the inheritance for the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.

The sixth lot was for Naphtali and its clans. Their border started from Heleph, from the oak tree at Zaanannim, passed Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan River. The border then went west at Aznoth Tabor and came out at Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and the Jordan River on the east. The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor, Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh—nineteen towns and their villages.
This was the inheritance for the tribe of Naphtali, the cities and their villages, clan by clan.

The seventh lot went to the tribe of Dan. The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh, Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon, Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the area facing Joppa.

But the people of Dan had a tough time; they couldn't drive out the Amorites, who pushed them back into the hill country. The Amorites kept them out of the plains, so they were running out of space. Because of this, the Danites marched up and attacked Leshem. They captured it, killed everyone inside, and settled there. They even renamed it Leshem Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of Dan, according to its clans, these towns with their villages.

After they finished dividing the land and setting the boundaries, the people of Israel gave a special inheritance to Joshua son of Nun. Following God's command, they gave him the city he asked for, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the city and settled down there.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral tribes assigned by lot to the tribes of Israel at Shiloh. They did this in the presence of God at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. And with that, they finished dividing the land.

title: God's Safe Zones: The OG No-Revenge Rule
paragraphs: So God hit up Joshua and was like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites to set up those safe zones we talked about with Moses. If someone accidentally kills a person—like, they didn't mean to—they can run to one of those cities to be safe from anyone trying to get revenge.'
If you're in that situation, you gotta book it to one of these cities, go to the main gate, and tell the city leaders what went down. They have to let you in and give you a place to crash.

And if the person trying to get revenge shows up, the leaders can't hand you over. It was an accident, you know? No bad blood. You can stay there until you have your trial and until the head priest dies. After that, you're free to go back home.
So they designated these cities: Kedesh in Galilee, in the hills of Naphtali, Shechem in the hills of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron) in the hills of Judah.

On the other side of the Jordan, east of Jericho, they picked Bezer on the desert plateau (from the tribe of Reuben), Ramoth in Gilead (from the tribe of Gad), and Golan in Bashan (from the tribe of Manasseh). These were the safe zones for all Israelites and any foreigners living with them. So if you accidentally killed someone, you could go there and not get taken out by an avenger before you even got a fair trial.

title: The Levites Finally Get Their Land!
paragraphs: So, the leaders of the Levite families went to meet with Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the other Israelite tribes. This all went down in Shiloh, in Canaan. They said, “Look, God commanded through Moses that you give us cities to live in, plus some pastureland for our cattle.”
So, the Israelites did what God said and gave the Levites cities and pastures from their own inherited land.

The first lot was for the Kohathite families. The Levites who were descendants of Aaron the priest got thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. The rest of the Kohathites got ten cities from the families of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The Gershonites got thirteen cities by lot from the families of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The Merarite families received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
So, the people of Israel gave these cities and their pastures to the Levites, just like God had ordered through Moses, by drawing lots.

From the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, they assigned the following towns, which are named here. These were for the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite branch of Levi, because they got the first pick:

Kiriath Arba (Arba was the ancestor of Anak), which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with its surrounding pastures. But the fields and villages around the city had already been given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his property.

So, to the descendants of Aaron the priest, they gave Hebron (which was a safe city for people who accidentally killed someone), Libnah, Jattir, Eshtemoa, Holon, Debir, Ain, Juttah, and Beth Shemesh, all with their pastures—nine towns from these two tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon, Geba, Anathoth, and Almon, along with their pastures—four towns.
The total for the priests descended from Aaron was thirteen cities with their pastures.

The rest of the Kohathite families from the tribe of Levi were given their cities by lot from the tribe of Ephraim: Shechem (another one of those safe cities) in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer, Kibzaim, and Beth Horon, with their pastures—four towns.
From the tribe of Dan, they got Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Aijalon, and Gath Rimmon, all with their pastures—four towns.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, they got Taanach and Gath Rimmon with their pastures—two towns.
All in all, the remaining Kohathite families got ten cities with their pastures.
The Gershonite families of the Levites were given from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan (another safe city), and Be Eshtarah, with their pastures—two cities.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En Gannim, with their pastures—four towns.
From the tribe of Asher: Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob, with their pastures—four towns.
From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee (a safe city), Hammoth Dor, and Kartan, with their pastures—three towns.
For the Gershonites and their families, it was thirteen towns with their pastures.
The Merari families, the last of the Levites, were given from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, and Nahalal, with their pastures—four cities.
From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer, Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath, with their pastures—four towns.
From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead (a safe city), Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Jazer, with their pastures—a total of four towns.
All these towns were given by lot to the Merarites, the rest of the Levites—twelve towns in total.
So, the Levites had forty-eight towns with their pastures inside the territory of the Israelites. Every single one of these towns had pastures around it.

And just like that, God gave Israel the entire land he had promised their ancestors. They took it over and settled down. And God gave them peace on all sides, just as he had promised their ancestors. Not a single one of their enemies could stand against them—God handed all their enemies over to them.
Not one of the good promises God made to the house of Israel failed. Everything came true.
