title: That Time We Almost Started a Civil War Over an Altar
paragraphs: So Joshua got the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh together and said, “You guys have done everything Moses, God’s servant, told you to do, and you’ve listened to everything I’ve commanded. You haven’t bailed on your brothers this whole time, right down to today. You’ve seriously shouldered the responsibility God gave you.

And now, your God has given your brothers some peace and quiet, just like he promised. So you’re free to go. Head back to your homes, to the land that Moses, God’s servant, gave you on the other side of the Jordan River. Just one thing: Be super careful to follow the Commandment and the rules Moses laid out for you: Love your God, walk in his ways, do what he says, stick close to him, and serve him with your whole heart and soul.”

Then Joshua blessed them and sent them off. They headed home. (Moses had given the half-tribe of Manasseh their land in Bashan. Joshua gave the other half their land with their brothers west of the Jordan.)

As Joshua sent them home, he blessed them again, saying, “Go on home. You’re going back rich—with tons of cattle, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and a huge amount of clothes. Make sure you share all that loot you got from your enemies with your family and friends!”

The guys from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the rest of the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan and started their journey back to Gilead, their own land that they had taken, just as God had commanded through Moses.

When they got to Geliloth by the Jordan River (which is right on the edge of Canaan), the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there on the riverbank—and it was a massive altar.

The rest of the Israelites heard about it, and the news was like, “Whoa, what’s this? The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar right across from us, facing Canaan at Geliloth on the Jordan!”

When the Israelites heard this, the whole community gathered at Shiloh, ready to go to war against them. They sent Phinehas, son of the priest Eleazar, to the land of Gilead to talk to the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Ten chiefs went with him, one from each of the ten tribes, each a leader of his family and representing the military divisions of Israel.

They went to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh and said, “The entire community of God wants to know: What is this betrayal against the God of Israel? You’ve turned your back on God by building your own altar. That’s straight-up rebellion against God! Wasn’t the whole Peor incident bad enough for us? We’re still dealing with the consequences of that plague on God’s people! And now you’re turning your back on God? If you rebel against God today, he’s going to be furious with the entire nation of Israel tomorrow.

“If you think your land isn’t holy enough or something, then come back over to God’s side of the river, where God’s own Dwelling is, and take some land there. But don’t rebel against God. And don’t rebel against us by building your own altar besides the one true Altar of our God. Remember when Achan, son of Zerah, messed with the sacred stuff? God’s anger came down on the whole community of Israel. He wasn’t the only one who died for his sin.”
The men of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the Israelite tribes:
“The God of all gods is God! The God of all gods is God!

“He knows, and we want all of Israel to know, if this was some rebellious betrayal of God. If it was, then don’t even bother trying to save us. If we built this altar to rebel against God, or to offer up our own big-time sacrifices and offerings, then let God himself be the judge.

“But that’s not why we did it. We did it because we were worried. We were scared that someday your kids would say to our kids, ‘You have no connection to God, the God of Israel! God put the Jordan River as a border between us and you. You Reubenites and Gadites have no part in God.’ And then your kids might make our kids stop worshiping God.
“So we said to ourselves, ‘Let’s do something. Let’s build an altar—but not for sacrifices or offerings.’

“We built this altar to be a witness between us and you, and for our kids who come after us. It’s a witness to the real Altar where we worship God at his sacred Dwelling with all our offerings and sacrifices.
“This way, your kids can’t say to our kids in the future, ‘You have no part in God.’

“We told ourselves, ‘If anyone ever says something like that to us or our kids in the future, we’ll say: Look at this replica of God’s Altar that our ancestors made. It’s not for sacrifices. It’s a witness that connects us with you.’

“Rebelling against God or turning our backs on him is the last thing we’d ever want to do. We never even dreamed of building another altar for offerings to compete with the Altar of our God that stands in front of his sacred Dwelling.”
Phinehas the priest, and all the leaders of the community and the military who were with him, heard what the men of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh had to say. And they were satisfied.

Priest Phinehas, son of Eleazar, said to them, “Okay, now we know for sure that God is with us, since you haven’t been disloyal to God in this. You’ve actually saved the people of Israel from God’s punishment.”

Then Phinehas and the chiefs left the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and went back to Canaan to give a full report to the People of Israel. They were happy with the report. The Israelites blessed God, and all the talk about attacking and destroying the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived stopped.
Reuben and Gad named the altar:
A Witness Between Us. God Alone Is God.

title: Joshua's Mic Drop: Stay Loyal or Get Wrecked
paragraphs: A super long time went by. God had given Israel a break from all the enemies around them, and Joshua was now a really, really old dude. So, he got all of Israel together—the elders, the leaders, the judges, all the important people. Then he laid it all out for them:
“Look, I’m old. I’ve been around forever. You guys literally saw everything God did to those other nations for you. He did it because he’s *your* God. He was fighting on your team.”

“And check it out: I’ve divvied up the land of the nations that are still left. It’s your inheritance now, from the Jordan River all the way to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. This includes the nations I already took down. Your God is gonna keep pushing them out of your way until they’re completely gone, and you’ll take over their land, just like he promised.”

“So, you gotta stay strong. Like, for real. Obey everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Don’t skip a single thing. Don’t even start chilling with the other nations still hanging around. Don’t say their gods' names, don't make promises using their names, and definitely do not worship or pray to them. You gotta stick with your God, just like you’ve been doing.”

“God has kicked out some majorly powerful nations for you. And so far, nobody has been able to stand up to you. Think about it—one of you could literally make a thousand enemies run for it! That’s because your God, he’s fighting for you, just like he said he would.”

“So, for real, guard your souls: Love your God. Because if you start to drift and get tangled up with the nations still living among you—like marrying them and just doing life with them—then you can be 100% sure that your God will stop clearing them out for you. They’ll become a total nightmare. It’ll be like getting whipped on your back and getting sand in your eyes, until you’re the ones who get kicked out of this amazing land that your God gave you.”

“Alright, you can all see I’m about to die, which is how everyone ends up. You need to know this with your whole heart, with everything you’ve got, that not a single good thing your God promised you has failed. It all came true. Not one word was dropped.”

“But just as every good promise from your God came true, he will also bring about every bad thing if you mess up. He’ll keep at it until there’s nothing left of you in this good land he gave you. If you break the covenant your God commanded, and you go off and serve and worship other gods, God’s anger will explode against you. And just like that, you’ll be gone. There won’t even be a trace of you left in this good land he gave you.”

title: The Ultimate Loyalty Test: Are You In or Out?
paragraphs: Joshua got all the tribes of Israel together at Shechem. He called in all the elders, chiefs, judges, and officers, and they all showed up before God. Then Joshua laid it all out for the people:

"Here's what God, the God of Israel, is saying: Way back in the day, your ancestors, Terah and his sons Abraham and Nahor, lived east of the Euphrates River. And yeah, they were into other gods. But I picked your ancestor Abraham from way over there, led him all through Canaan, and gave him a huge family. I gave him Isaac. Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir for his own, but Jacob and his sons had to go down to Egypt. So I sent Moses and Aaron, hit Egypt with some major plagues, and then I led you guys out. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you got to the sea. But the Egyptians were right on your tail with chariots and cavalry, chasing you all the way to the Red Sea!
"Then you guys cried out to God for help. So He threw up a cloud between you and the Egyptians and then just let the sea crash down on them. They all drowned.

"You saw the whole thing go down with your own eyes, what I did to Egypt. After that, you lived in the wilderness for a long time. Then I brought you into the land of the Amorites, who lived east of the Jordan, and they tried to fight you. But I had your back and you took their land. I totally wiped them out for you. Then this guy Balak, son of Zippor, the king of Moab, showed up. He was getting ready to throw down with Israel and even sent for Balaam son of Beor to come and curse you. But I wasn't having it. I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and he ended up blessing you like crazy instead! I saved you from him.

"Then you crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The leaders of Jericho, plus the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites all ganged up on you, but I handed them all over to you.
"I sent the Hornet out ahead of you, and it drove out the two Amorite kings. It basically did all the work for you. You didn't have to lift a finger.
"I gave you land you didn't even work for and towns you didn't build. And now you're living in them, eating from vineyards and olive groves you didn't even plant.

"So here's the deal: Fear God. Serve him and be 100% committed. Get rid of all the fake gods your ancestors were into on the other side of the Euphrates and in Egypt. You guys need to worship the real God.

"But if you think serving God is a bad idea, then you need to choose today who you're going to serve. Go ahead, pick one. Maybe one of the gods your ancestors worshiped way back when, or one of the gods of the Amorites, since you're living in their land now. But as for me and my house, we're sticking with God."
The people shot back, "No way we'd ever ditch God! Never! We'd never leave God for other gods.

"God is our God! He's the one who brought our ancestors out of Egypt where they were slaves. He did all those insane miracles right in front of us. He's watched over us this whole time, on all the roads we've traveled and through all the nations we've passed. He drove out all those other nations, including the Amorites, just for us.
"So count us in. We're going to serve God too. He's our God."

But Joshua told the people, "Honestly, you can't do it. You're not capable of serving God. He's a holy God, and He's a jealous God. He's not going to put up with you messing around and sinning. If you leave God and start worshiping foreign gods, He'll turn on you and bring you down. He'll finish you, even after all the good stuff He's done for you!"
But the people insisted, "No! Seriously! We will serve God!"
So Joshua said to them, "You're witnesses against yourselves that you've chosen God—to serve him."
And they all said, "Yep, we're witnesses."
Joshua said, "Okay then, get rid of all the foreign gods you have stashed away. Give a full-hearted 'Yes' to God, the God of Israel."
The people answered Joshua, "We will serve God. Whatever He says, we'll do."

So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day in Shechem. He made it official, spelling out all the rules. He wrote it all down in the Book of God's Law. Then he took a massive stone and set it up under the oak tree in God's holy place.
Joshua said to all the people, "See this stone? It's a witness against us. It heard every single word God said to us. So it's a witness against you, in case you try to cheat on your God."
Then Joshua sent everyone home, each to their own land.
After all this, Joshua, son of Nun, God's servant, died. He was 110 years old. They buried him in his own land at Timnath Serah in the mountains of Ephraim, just north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served God during Joshua's entire lifetime, and also during the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him, who had seen for themselves everything God had done for Israel.

And Joseph's bones, which the Israelites had carried all the way from Egypt, were buried in Shechem. It was in the piece of land that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor (Shechem's dad) for a hundred silver coins. That land is part of the inheritance of Joseph's family.
Then Eleazar, Aaron's son, died. They buried him at Gibeah, a town that had been given to his son Phinehas in the mountains of Ephraim.
